review.summary: This paper presents a retrospective empirical evaluation of two recent annual satellite embedding products—AlphaEarth Foundations V1 mosaic and TESSERA v1—for screening one-year tree-cover transitions (gains and losses) in the conterminous United States (CONUS) using LCMAP and Annual NLCD reference labels, conditional on a known initial cover class. Specifically, the study tests whether updating reference-forest embeddings annually (concurrent references) or subtracting mean changes from independent tree control plots improves transition classification at transferred 10% nominal false-positive-rate thresholds compared with a fixed start-year reference and supervised classifiers. Across both embedding products and datasets, reference and control adjustments produce negligible changes in Youden's J (-0.037 to +0.011), leave 90.8-98.5% of test alert decisions unchanged, maintain very high rank correlations (Spearman 0.947-0.996), and flip signs across alternative calibration partitions. Diagnostics show that this null result occurs because CONUS-wide reference centroids move very little between adjacent years and subtracting a regional control mean is an algebraic constant within each region-year stratum. More importantly, the study uncovers a stark operational asymmetry between one-year tree loss and one-year tree gain: while unsupervised cosine change magnitude strongly discriminates tree loss (AUROC 0.956-0.968), it detects 0 of 24 tree gains in both products and exhibits an inverted ranking (AUROC 0.287-0.318), as one-year gain plots exhibit smaller embedding changes than unchanged grass and shrub plots. Furthermore, input ablations and reference-similarity scatter plots reveal that the much higher gain discrimination of subsequent-state and direct supervised classifiers (AUROC 0.759-0.907) is largely driven by baseline pre-transition proximity to the tree reference rather than inter-annual embedding movement.

score_reasons.correctness: All empirical claims, statistical intervals, and algebraic identities are rigorously verified and scrupulously qualified, though the primary control-mean adjustment is a constant shift within region-year strata and an intended paired native-grid check remains unfinished.
score_reasons.verifiability: The paper provides exceptional methodological transparency, including exact numerators and denominators for every split, mathematical definitions of all scores, public data provenance, deterministic seeds, and pre-specified protocol records.
score_reasons.novelty: While directional change vector analysis, control centering, and conditional state classification are established techniques, the side-by-side diagnostic evaluation of AlphaEarth V1 and TESSERA v1—particularly the discovery of the gain-magnitude ranking inversion and baseline-state dominance—is new and timely.
score_reasons.generality: Empirical generality is heavily constrained by the tiny and temporally concentrated positive sample for tree gains (only 24 LCMAP test gains, with 21 in 2019-2020 and 3 in 2020-2021), the single-year transition horizon, and the use of broadly pooled CONUS references rather than local ecological references.
score_reasons.usefulness: The findings offer high practical value for remote-sensing and restoration monitoring teams by demonstrating that annual embedding change magnitude fails on one-year tree gains and that apparent supervised gain detection largely reflects initial-state proximity rather than inter-annual change.
score_reasons.clarity: Readability is substantially hampered by defensive audit-log prose, repetitive methodological disclaimers, inline file-path references, meta-commentary on AI review revisions, and the relegation of key mechanistic insights (Figures 3 and 4) to the appendices.

research_question.question: In CONUS one-year land-cover pairs with supplied initial cover classes, do year-matched references or independent control-plot mean adjustments improve tree-cover gain and loss screening over a fixed start-year reference and supervised classifiers?
research_question.predictable_reason: It was algebraically and geometrically predictable that subtracting a regional control mean preserves within-stratum rankings and that averaging ~50 reference plots across CONUS yields minimal annual centroid drift, whereas the empirical inversion of cosine change magnitude on tree gains and the cross-product comparison required empirical testing.

main_issues.issue: Small and temporally skewed gain sample: The primary LCMAP test set contains only 24 tree-gain positives (21 in 2019-2020 and just 3 in 2020-2021), and the NLCD 2022-2023 extension contains only 7 gain positives, which severely limits statistical power for evaluating spatial and temporal transfer on tree gains.

Weak primary correction design: Reference centroids are averaged over 39-53 plots across CONUS (with the 8th-nearest reference still a median 1,071 km away), smoothing out local inter-annual phenological drift, and global control-mean subtraction is constant within each region-year pair, making it an inherently weak test of local reference/control adjustment.

Defensive audit-log presentation and buried mechanistic insights: The manuscript reads like a compliance log filled with meta-disclaimers, repository file paths, and revision notes, while the most compelling scientific insight—that gain positives already sit near the forest cluster at t0 and barely move over one year (Figure 4 and Appendix D)—is buried in exploratory appendices.

Unfinished native-grid paired check: The manuscript prominently retains an incomplete paired native-grid experiment (0/16 complete pairs acquired) in the title header, main text, and Appendix C/F; this unfinished check should either be completed by fetching the missing native COGs or removed.

Potential pretraining target overlap for AlphaEarth: As acknowledged in Section 3.2, AlphaEarth V1 used NLCD weak supervision during encoder training, which confounds the interpretation of supervised state classifiers on the NLCD and LCMAP endpoints, though TESSERA v1 provides a clean self-supervised contrast.

strengths: Rigorous, transparent experimental hygiene with full disclosure of negative results, partition sensitivities, exact subgroup denominators, and conditional block bootstrap intervals.

Important practical finding that annual embedding cosine magnitude (1 - a·b) strongly detects one-year tree loss (AUROC > 0.95) but exhibits an inverted ranking on one-year tree gain (AUROC 0.29-0.35, smaller change than unchanged grass/shrubs).

Revealing input-ablation and reference-similarity diagnostics (Figures 3 and 4) showing that high gain AUROC in subsequent-state and direct learners stems primarily from pre-change baseline embeddings (before-only vector a) rather than inter-annual change vectors (b - a).

Direct, reproducible comparison across two distinct geospatial foundation models (supervised/multi-modal AlphaEarth V1 mosaic vs. self-supervised Sentinel-1/2 TESSERA v1) and two reference label schemas (LCMAP and Annual NLCD).

closest_prior_work.citation: Heiman, A. (2026). Characterizing Brazilian Atlantic Forest Restoration Outcomes with Geospatial AlphaEarth Embeddings. arXiv:2605.05547, ICLR ML4RS Workshop.
closest_prior_work.difference: Heiman (2026) introduces reference trajectory cosine similarity using AlphaEarth embeddings for multi-year forest restoration in Brazil, whereas the present paper tests fixed, year-matched, and control-adjusted reference similarity for one-year tree-cover transitions in CONUS against supervised and state-only baselines across both AlphaEarth and TESSERA.

closest_prior_work.citation: Brown, C. F., Kazmierski, M. R., Pasquarella, V. J., et al. (2025). AlphaEarth Foundations: An embedding field model for accurate and efficient global mapping from sparse label data. arXiv:2507.22291.
closest_prior_work.difference: Brown et al. (2025) introduce AlphaEarth Foundations and evaluate angular embedding change on LCMAP with validation-tuned thresholds, whereas this paper evaluates spatio-temporally transferred thresholds calibrated on earlier negatives, separates directional reference scores from magnitude, and adds TESSERA v1 and NLCD comparisons.

closest_prior_work.citation: Burns, M. (2026). Rethinking Change Detection and Attribution: How You Compare Satellite Embeddings Matters. Google Earth and Earth Engine Medium Case Study.
closest_prior_work.difference: Burns (2026) presents a qualitative/case-study comparison of dot products, difference vectors, and stacked annual AlphaEarth embeddings for landscape change attribution, whereas this study provides a formal quantitative evaluation with held-out spatio-temporal calibration, reference/control adjustments, and TESSERA v1 comparisons.

closest_prior_work.citation: Feng, Z., Atzberger, C., Jaffer, S., et al. (2026). TESSERA: Temporal Embeddings of Surface Spectra for Earth Representation and Analysis. arXiv:2506.20380.
closest_prior_work.difference: Feng et al. (2026) introduce the self-supervised TESSERA annual embedding product and benchmark downstream classification/regression, whereas this paper evaluates TESSERA v1 alongside AlphaEarth V1 specifically on transferred one-year tree-cover gain and loss screening.

closest_prior_work.citation: Ball, J. G. C., et al. (2026). Geospatial foundation models enable data-efficient tree species mapping in temperate mountain forests. Science of Remote Sensing, 100466.
closest_prior_work.difference: Ball et al. (2026) examine cross-year temporal transfer of tree-species classifiers using geospatial foundation-model embeddings, whereas this paper investigates bitemporal tree-cover transition screening and tests whether reference-centroid or control-plot adjustments improve transferred threshold decisions.
